title: Good quality, holds a lot but color lighter than expected
text:
I got the extra-large basket and the dimensions posted are accurate. The basket was shipped flat and folded. I don’t mind having to do a little work to reshape because I figure I am doing a small part to protect our natural resources and environment by using less packaging. The first day, I folded the basket in the opposite directions. The next day, I stuffed it full of blankets and towels. It has shaped up fairly well. While it is not fully round at this point, I am satisfied for now the way it is because it stands upright. I think it will adjust gradually as it gets used but if not, then I will drag out my iron.

The basket is well made, with no loose stitches, and is thick and strong. I like the hidden handles that I can just slide my hands into. They make the basket comfortable to hold, I won’t worry that the weight of the filled basket will be too heavy for the handles, and I like that the handles are out of the way until I want to use them. I ordered the basket in Graphite and was expecting it to be black or nearly black, from the pictures. But the plastic bag that held the folded basket said ‘gray’, and it does look like a dark gray. I was going to send it back but after looking at the web site and seeing that they have a graphite l and a graphite ll and a gray, which was a light gray, I decided to just keep the basket I received. Photo colors can be inaccurate and monitors vary, but I would say the true color is somewhere between the shades that are in the two photos I posted.

title: Large changing pad for toddler
text:
Overall, I am pleased with this product. The quality is good and I especially like the size of this pad. I use mine every time I have my grandson, whether it’s at home or when we are out in the park or at restaurants or wherever we are out and about. It is easy to wipe. I always wipe the pad after each use then I fold the each ends toward the center vertically this way the white side are not touching the black side. I then fold the black ends again vertically toward the center and finally I fold the black ends horizontally. This creates a square and it fits in my diaper bag perfectly! This is the only way I can be assured the inside does not touch the outside part. It’s important when my grandson is laying on top of the white side, that it is clean and has no germs. When I am out and about, I use baby wipes to wipe the pad. But if I am at home I first use baby wipes then I use my hand wipes with antiseptic to wipe the pad again and then I leave it open to let it air dry. I have had mines for several months and it’s holding up well! I am a satisfied customer!

The only negative comment is that the strap is not positioned to where I can use it to close the pad with the Velcro strap. I just let it hang. I have not cut the strap off because I am afraid it will create a sharp edge and I don’t want it to become unsightly. I wish they would have provided information on how to fold using the strap to close. The inside or the white side should not touch the outside or the black side.

text:

There are three screens for you to see your baby. 2 at the top and when your kiddo is laying down, to almost completely flat I might add, there is a huge mesh screen that unzips to allow for air flow. I always ended up with a sweaty baby so I'm hopeful this will help! I'm not sure why the other reviewers complained about the straps...it's a 5 point harness. Also, the stroller weighs nothing. It is so light and compact.

I bought the snack tray and standing board separately (waiting for those to arrive), which is fine. A lot, if not most, strollers nowadays don't include these accessories I'm noticing. I had a cup holder thing from another stroller that I attached to the handle bar without any issues.

The basket. It is not easily accessible. There is a bar going across the back of the stroller so I'm not even sure how to squeeze things over or under the bar to get to the basket. You can see it in photos, I missed it. That is my only issue, because I like to put the diaper bag in there, but then again I guess that is not the purpose of this lightweight compact stroller. Is it a deal breaker? No. The stroller is awesome and I'm going to keep it for the pros outweigh the con.

title: Flimsy plastic, not really 3 in 1
text: There are several pegs with barbs that lock into the first step. While assembling, two of the barbs popped right off when inserting into the holes. I returned it for a replacement. The gray inserts of each step are made of hard plastic, not rubber or any type of grippy surface. It may not be intentional, but the images are misleading by making the inserts gray to insinuate that it's Ade of rubber like most stools. The stool is marketed as 3 in 1, but it's really difficult to disassemble the segments... and after experiencing how fragile the bars are on the locking pegs, I wouldn't want to take it apart for fear that they would all snap. Even if you decide to do so, you would need a screwdriver or pliers to move each barb to get the peg free. On top of all this, the plastic buckles slightly under the weight of our 3 yo. It is too thin to handle anything over 25 lbs imo. Our toddler slipped the first time using this because she was wearing socks and the gray top is slippery. She now won't use it without asking for someone to hold her hand now. Maybe passable for some toddlers that are very small, but generally you don't want to have to worry about slipping or flimsiness in a toddler stool.

title: Just okay
text:
First, as another reviewer noted, you need your upper and lower measurements to be in the same measurement angle that correlates with each wing addition to the gate. Our baseboard level distance was in one range and the wall to wall distance was in the next higher range which meant we needed to cut blocks of wood to use as flat shims on the top. If I was using this with a baby or toddler, I’d have sent it straight back as the need for shimming makes the gate less secure against the walls. However, I’m only using this to keep an injured dog from going upstairs while his surgery heals, so it’ll do.

I do like the gate part. It’s got nice clearance for going through. The latch isn’t all that great, though. A clever toddler or big dog could knock it open easily. Mine is pretty loose but that’s because we’re using it on stairs with one side fastened against the stair rails. I don’t want to force the rails out of alignment, so we’re making do.

Setting it up was not easy. The hinge side goes on just fine. It’s the latch side. That’s because the upright requires a great deal of force to keep it vertical while setting the pressure screws. It really needs two people to get it right and tight. I will say that a big part of my difficulties sprang from the top and bottom measurements falling in different size ranges. If your measurements are in the same range, you’ll likely have a much easier time.

Like I said, it will do the job. Would I buy this again? Nope. Would I use this with a baby or toddler? Nope. Both my boys figured out baby locks on cabinets by the age of 1. They would have had no problem operating the latch on the gate, which pretty much defeats the purpose. So, an okay gate for even spaces but tricky if you have baseboards.

10/10!

title: There's a trick to hanging this nicely designed child's growth scroll
text:
At the current price of $39.99, this is expensive but it is a lovely scroll and very attractive. It also has a hole for a marker on the top side where it hangs. However, in order for this to work, one has to read the instructions.

The idea is to pick one of the foot or centimeter marks on the scroll and line it up to the distance measured from the floor with a measuring tape. For instance, let's say I pick 5 feet from the floor. I should mark that position on my wall using a measuring tape. When done, I then line up the 5 foot mark on the scroll with that line. Both lines have to match when I hang the scroll. This way everything will be the correct distance from the floor when using the scroll to mark off a child's height.

This is a lovely scroll and it provides an independent record of a child's growth without having to mark up the house wall.

First of all, the packaging that the item comes in, mentions that it is a tent/mosquito net for kids, but does not mention that it is for cribs. It definitely seems like it was repurposed and sold outside of its intended purposes.
Second, the install instructions on the packaging and on the description sheet inserted into the product are different from each other.
Lastly, the material was not taught in a full size crib. It would be very easy for an infant to inhale and choke on the netting.

As for the packaging description of a tent/mosquito net, it would do a decent job as a stand-alone product. However, there is a 2" square hole at the top where the poles cross, so I'm not sure how that would affect its viability.

title: Learned As We Went
text:
This was my first time trying cloth and here are some things I learned:

Most important: if your baby has thick thighs, the second gusset could be a curse more than a blessing. The raw elastic rubbed by baby’s thighs raw once she got bigger so we had to go with something else after 4 months of using.

You could probably use these diapers on a newborn but you will need either newborn inserts or something like flour sack towels. We decided to wait until 2 months. Everything was big but fit.

Breastfed babies will have leaking at the seams of the diaper but as long as you change it soon after a poop you’ll be set.

It’s easier said than done to just change out inserts. We bought an insert for each diaper.

These shells are easy to clean since they don’t really hold anything. If the white parts get poop stains then leave them in the sun after washing and you’re golden.

All in all I like them and really tried to make these work but they just ended up hurting my baby. Now we’re rockin pockets

title: Made for the easiest transition to formula!
text:
I am so relieved I found this for when my baby was switching from exclusively breastmilk to formula. I was stressed out when the frozen milk I had stored up was running out, and this made it so easy.

I love how quick and easy making a bottle is and since the water is constantly at the same temp, my baby doesn't have to wait long when they want milk...which is also nice for mommy and daddy since that means less crying. My baby likes things on the warmer side, so although he took his formula on the middle(orange) setting, once we tested the red setting and knew it was fine for him to have, he seemed to like that more AND it really helps the formula dissolve in the water much easier.

I love that it doesn't take up much counter space and it can be used for other beverages as well(hot tea, hot chocolate, warm lemon water, etc.)

Only thing I don't like is that it cannot be submerged in water and the water tank doesn't come off the base, so cleaning is a little tough but doable. I noticed this is a common thing with all water tanks like this though, so it's not specific to just this one.

All in all I would DEFINITELY recommend this to someone wanting warm/hot water available on demand!

title: Good for sorting and storing small items
text:
I spent a little time with these baskets before completing my review because I was curious to see how I put them to use.
The reason I waited is because these are relatively shallow fabric baskets, which makes them very different from the decorative storage items I already own.
Well, I am happy to report that these are turning out to be extremely helpful little baskets, both in terms storage and sorting a wide variety of objects.

That second function of sorting caught me a bit by surprise, but it is an important one.
If you have a job, a hobby, or even a regular household task that involves sorting, these baskets might be the thing you didn't know you needed.
The reason these are so good for sorting is that they are wide enough to give you a surface to sort on, with sides tall enough to keep what your sorting contained, all without being so tall it makes working inside the basket difficult.
Consequently, coins, beads, stones, accessories, and various other bric-a-brac can be sorted within or among baskets with ease.

My obsession with using these as sorting baskets aside, they also make excellent storage.
I imagine anyone looking to neaten up a changing table or a sock drawer would be thrilled with these.
That also makes them a nice gift option.
Add a few baby related items to these and you will have a shower gift someone will both appreciate and actually use.

The low profile of these baskets, combined with the built in handles, also make them a great option for using on shelves and inside drawers.
Almost any small to medium sized objects (keys, coins, undies...) that you access regularly, but want to keep corralled, are going to be a good fit for one of these baskets.
That makes them a quick and appealing way to enhance organization in a closet, armoire, or bureau.

These affordable, sturdy, appealing, and functional Stellaberry baskets are a real find; definitely recommend!

text:

The pillow was extremely clean and fresh.

The bunny is sweet. There are long ears and a tiny little face in the corner of the pillow. I like that the pillow is rectangular and it does fit nicely on the bed. It is fluffy but not too big which I prefer for children’s pillows. Also it’s not memory foam but more of a very soft almost feather type of bedding but it’s fluff like a poly fill. The metal ones are always cumbersome, some fold down, some don't, some are wobbly, others are inflatable and leak air, some move all over the place....this one has seriously been perfect. The foam makes it easy to get on and off the bed (as an adult) without having to crawl off the bottom of the bed. It also stays in place under the sheets and we have not had any issues of it falling, slipping or even being kicked out of place by our kids. The foam is soft enough to rest your head, but stiff enough to keep the wiggly worms on the bed. The rails come packaged rolled up in a tight air-sealed plastic. As soon as you cut it open they unroll and puff up like magic - then you simply put them under the sheet. Seriously the easiest thing I did all month. Definitely recommend!!

title: Borderline Dangerous
text:
I have been using this tub for 16 weeks. The stickers flaked off early on, but they are gone now and don't bother us. My sling also hasn't gotten moldy like some others. My biggest complaint is that the 1st configuration wasn't useful for very long for my longer baby. He started kicking himself mostly out of the tub. We then had to switch to configuration 2 at 4 months, but it isn't supportive enough to keep him from wigging down into the tub and potentially submerging his head into the water. It hasn't happened but he sinks down so quickly that it easily could if my husband and I didn't both participate in bath time. We have to hold his butt in place in the sling so he doesn't slide down and drown in while the other bathes him. It just feels really dangerous for babies in that in between stage of not sitting up alone but being too big for the newborn configuration. Perhaps if your baby is tiny and doesn't wiggle it wouldn't be an issue. It's unfortunate,too, because my baby loves the tub. He kicks and splashes and laughs...although that's what causes him to slide. We will be looking for a new option. I guess there's a reason it needs so many warning stickers.
Btw, I tried also posting this on the skip hop website and they wouldn't publish it, so I wouldn't trust their rating at all. They, instead, sent me an email trying to get me to set up a phone meeting about the safety issue.

title: GATE WONT FULLY OPEN (SOLVED)
text:
The gate is fine but I must give it 1 star for poor instructions that have caused others grief.
Step 8 of instructions are key!
Step 8 is misleading and easy to miss. The instruction suggests you adjust the bolts to make things even.
WRONG! You MUST unscrew the “eye” bolt. It comes fully screwed into the gate, this will NOT WORK. Unscrew the eye bolt about 3/4” until you can test mount the hinge and verify rotates +/- 90 degrees.
If you dont do this, after installation when you try to open the gate you will break the top hinge or it out of the wall.
Photo #1. As it comes (will not work)
Photo #2. Eye bolt unscrewed so hinge can fully rotate.

text:
scent: it has a strange scent at first (i expected no scent or obvious rose) but i have to say it grew on me. and like many ‘natural’ products without strong fragrances it takes a little time to get used to and then is quite pleasant

dangerous ingredients: the combination of sodium benzoate and vitamin c - my research turned up some studies that indicate a negative reaction between these chemicals (often used in food and cosmetic products to reduce the chance of mold/mildew/spoilage); however, they must be exposed to high heat or light for such an effect, or be used in very large quantities/concentration. so don’t boil this soap or allow your baby to eat it all. seems straightforward enough.

doesn’t do anything: this was my biggest objection at first. it doesn’t lather, and so it doesn’t feel satisfying as a cleanser. at first. i did get used to it and it definitely left my baby clean so i kept using it despite the disappointing feeling of no bubbles. then i tried another baby wash (honest). it was sudsy but left the most unbelievable film. i thought my child was going to slide right out of my arms. that’s when my appreciation for this product skyrocketed. i gained a whole new admiration for this soap and it’s non-frothy, non-overly-‘moisturizing’ results. i didn’t try other ‘edible’ baby soaps to compare but i do value highly that this one is safe because my baby likes to put her hands in her mouth in the shower and sometimes i can’t wash them off before she does so.

bottom line: an excellent product that i had to come back for.

title: Amazing Backpack! Exceeded expectations!
text:
This diaper bag/backpack has it all: function, style, storage and quality! We bought this backpack to use for family outings and hikes. We're past the diaper stage but were in the market for a nice neutral looking backpack and this one caught our eye because of how it looks. We chose the gray color and it looks even better than expected! Very stylish!! We just got it but used it for a nice long hike today and could not be happier.

It feels like whomever designed it put so much thought into the nice creature comforts that we didn't even expect. It has so much storage inside (and outside) that each of us had our own independent areas for storage! It has a nice removable bottle bag and we used that to keep our snacks cold with a small ice pack.

Other things that we love about it are 1) the wipe/tissue pocket, 2) the anti-theft back side pocket to secure phones and keys, 3) the usb charging port (OMG so convenient!!) and 4) how the backpack stays upright while sitting on the table for loading and unloading! No flopping over. It sits up by itself.

It has nice cushioning on the straps and the back too. That made it super comfortable to carry all day long. The zippers appear to be high quality and durable. We also love the brown leatherish zipper pulls.

Like I said, it seems like someone put a TON of thought into this bag. Our expectations were pretty high and they have been far exceeded. Kudos to the manufacturer of this awesome backpack/diaper bag/travel bag.

title: Ground control to Major Tom
text:
It's 4:27am. Our baby has been fussy, fidgety and sleepless all night. As a Hail Mary, we decided to give Frida's ingenious indigestion engines a try.

It's true, the tip inserts comfortably, the material is flexible, and you can't insert too far.

For t-minus fifteen seconds, nothing happened. I was sure we had failure to launch, and my wife was preparing for extraction, when...

Lift-off.

With a roar explosive enough to wake the neighborhood dogs, our son's "liquid fuel" instantly accelerated to a truly impressive velocity. I'm not sure if it broke the sound barrier, or if the resulting boom is just a natural side effect of the design, butt either way, the focused fecal jet-stream which burst forth from our pride and joy contained sufficient power that it would likely inspire the launch of a new space program in many countries.

Luckily, the junior asstronaut was strapped firmly to the changing table and we thus avoided losing our burbling baby boy to low-orbit. Unluckily, and, based on retrospective analysis, likely resulting from the combination of her sleep deprivation and me using her as a human blast shield, my wife hadn't quite cleared the launch pad at ignition. Her outline is still visible as an afterimage on the opposite wall.

Once the internal fuel tank had been fully spent and I felt safe enough to emerge and marvel at the aftermath, I watched in awe as our bundle of joy peacefully settled back to earth and slept like he'd been placed in suspended animation for an insterstellar voyage.

I whole-heartedly recommend this product for alleviating gas (and potentially changing its state of matter to hot plasma). I do, however, recommend fully clearing the launch site before insertion and perhaps donning an EVA suit before any attempt to shoot the moon. My wife will, I'm sure, agree, once we've resumed communications.

title: Remarkable way to capture memories – difficult to carry out!
text:
Baby Hand and Footprint Ink Kit, Keepsake Kit, New Mom, Newborn Gift (Black)

I have mixed feelings on this kit.

Positives:
• Comes in a cute box (so giftable)
• Simple to follow instructions
• The inkpad is easy to use
• There are five or so pages available for do-overs

*******************************
Negatives:

There are only five or so pages available for mistakes.

There is not a lot of space for both a handprint and a footprint. It’s not a well thought out design to have both on one page. If you get a decent footprint and then the handprint is crud – you’ve wasted the paper AND the good footprint – it’s maddening.

It’d be more efficient to have a separate square for each and plenty of uh-oh pages.

The ink goes everywhere and is harder to take off than expected. It got on baby’s head, chest, and legs (besides his hands and feet lol). It also got on the parents.

*******************************
Advice:

Try to plan this out. We thought we had a generous number of extra papers. We didn’t. We had a paper shortage – more of having to pick the “best of” versus the two best versions on one paper. Start with the handprint because that is the hardest to get from a newborn. Prepare to clean up a mess, yourself, your helpers, and baby.

As I said before, this kit is a remarkable way to capture memories – it is difficult to carry out.

title: Great for Between Showering
text:
Updated Review:
I ordered these in November and it's now January 1st. I was sick all of December, first with an upper respiratory infection (head cold), and on top of that a bacterial infection attacked my lungs, then a week later, I got sick with Covid! Being so sick, I wasn't able to shower as frequently as I prefer, and the fevering (for both viral infections and the bacterial infection) got me nasty sweaty.

These wipes came in very handy! I was able to wet them with warm water from my tap (below freezing temps in my area, while sick) and clean the important parts (lady bits, under breasts, arm pits, inner elbows, tummy, etc) before crawling back into bed.

Because of the convenience during one of the worst sick times I've had in years, I have increased from 3 stars to 4 stars. I can't rate these a 5, because when I do wet them with plain well water, there's a chemical odor. I haven't had a negative reaction, yet, but I do find this to be concerning and a potential drawback for persons who are more sensitive than I am.

So far, I'm pleased with these dry wipes. Simple, easy, and convenient. I do recommend giving these a try.

End Updated Review

~~~~~~~~
Original Review:

My photos tend to get lost, so I'm uploading the photos now; will write review after using.

In the meantime, the English translation is pretty funny and I got a kick out of "be careful not to eat by mistake." 😂

Perferated top for easy opening; no reclosing, as it becomes similar to tissue box or dried out wipes. Packed well. No odor! 🙌🏻 I'm very sensitive to scents and odors, so I'm glad there's none while dry. I did purchase for myself, an adult; if product works well for me, I'll see how it does for my grandson.

Dry sheet is softer than a paper towel or dryer sheet (another reviewer said it was the same -- it's not). Feels clean to the touch and soft. I'm looking forward to using these for in-between shower time clean ups.

I will rerate & update review at a later time. Meanwhile, I hope the pics are helpful.
